liveProofCredentialFree.isolation: the real ~/.mpd/workmate bytes are unchanged across the run (name+size+mtime fingerprint before/after), not asserted absent — the directory legitimately pre-exists

measurementsThatCorrectedThePlan.claim: an in-session mpd_role_spawn call can prove the fix
measurementsThatCorrectedThePlan.finding: FALSE, and this is the captain's own §N2: plugin code loads at BOOT, so a long-running session keeps the pre-fix module and keeps reporting the old error after the file is fixed

measurementsThatCorrectedThePlan.claim: in a fresh process a credential failure is positive evidence the list was accepted
measurementsThatCorrectedThePlan.finding: REFUTED by measurement: authentication happens BEFORE the child is composed. With a dummy key the run dies at `AUTH: Authentication Fails` and mpd_role_spawn is never attempted, so a credential error says nothing about the restriction list

measurementsThatCorrectedThePlan.claim: the pre-fix list fails against the real harness (acceptance criterion 2)
measurementsThatCorrectedThePlan.finding: NOT REPRODUCIBLE here. The same drive run against a pristine f697088 worktree sent the NINE-name list (including both unregistered names) to the harness and the child was still created and answered — no refusal. Measured in both directions with the adapter probe, so the list really was delivered. The genuine in-session failure and this measurement differ in process lifetime, which is consistent with a module-cache effect on the running host

measurementsThatCorrectedThePlan.claim: the child receives UNKNOWN_TOOL if it attempts a write (acceptance criterion 4)
measurementsThatCorrectedThePlan.finding: NOT DEMONSTRATED. The restriction demonstrably reaches the harness, but the child's own model request carries no tools array under this stub, so no child-side write attempt could be observed. Proving it needs a child-side tool-call turn
